blocked_reason: No second appliance with a different Incus package exists. The catalog has one qualified entry, alpine-3.24.2-lts-1 (incus 7.0.1-r2). The only other appliance build, the draft release alpine-3.24.2-stable-1 (static build evidence only, unqualified), ships the same incus-7.0.1-r2 and differs in its kernel (7.1.5-0-stable) and ZFS module, which the design classifies as reversible. Task 5.4 stays open until an appliance with another Incus package is qualified.

substitute.scenario: Migrating upgrade between the same appliance, forced by a recorded Incus package older than the catalog's, with the data clone, a refused rollback without the discard flag, a rollback restoring the data copy, and the restored state booting
substitute.method: With the runtime ready, incus_package in runtime/guest-record.json was changed from 7.0.1-r2 to 7.0.0-r2, written atomically at mode 0600. The planner reads the record on every plan, so the upgrade classified as migrating.

findings: Rollback without --discard-data-since-upgrade prints 'Stopping the runtime to restore the latest backup…' before the refusal, although the runtime is never stopped (it stays ready). Fixed after this run: the line now reads 'Checking the latest backup; the runtime is stopped only if it can be restored…' (unit test migratingUpgradeShowsWhatHappensBeforeTheStopAndRollbackNeedsTheDiscardFlag); the hardware run was not repeated with the new wording.

When the data copy is the backup's own, the refusal names the backup twice: 'Rolling back to backup X restores the data disk copy taken at T (backup X)'. Fixed after this run: a second backup is named only when the copy comes from a later one, as 'the data disk copy from backup Y taken at T' (unit tests discardWarningNamesWhenTheDataCopyWasTaken and rollbackAcrossALaterMigrationUsesTheLaterDataCopy).

After the rollback, start re-observed the restored develop root from the catalog and recorded incus 7.0.1-r2, replacing the forged 7.0.0-r2 from the backup. The safety backup therefore lists as restorable root only. That matches this run's real package. With two appliances of different IDs, the catalog would not know the old appliance and the restored record's package would become unknown; nothing here exercised that.
